run: the first listening test: blind A/B judgements on the sealed Neyshekar set's unseen speakers
status: registered 2026-10-03, before anyone has listened; no result is written until listeners have answered
why: every judgement in this project so far is an encoder's (held-out similarity) or a recogniser's (CER); nobody has listened. SOTA_ROADMAP section 3.4: a blind test is the only way to know whether a similarity difference is audible, and the only thing that could justify the 0.0205 line as a decision bar or retire it

systems.b: OmniVoice adapted, the export at step 1,000 (the sealed test's candidate)

sealed-published-vs-adapted.what_the_metric_said: +0.0014 [-0.0042, +0.0069] held-out similarity on these speakers: no detectable difference

systems.b: F5-TTS Persian at 48 steps (the arms session's renders)

sealed-omnivoice-vs-f5.what_the_metric_said: about +0.11 held-out similarity for OmniVoice on these speakers - the largest gap measured here

selection: seed 20261003: the 27 usable Neyshekar test speakers (ney06's reference is refused) shuffled; the first 14 to the first test, the next 7 to the second; one text per speaker drawn from t01-t12 without t11 (a one-second sentence - who is speaking cannot be judged from it); the seed-42 renders. Drawn before any clip was heard
each_trial: a real recording of the speaker that neither system was prompted with (the first held-out clip, never the prompt), then the two systems' renders of the same text in an order balanced across trials and hidden from the listener, all matched to -26 LUFS by gain alone, 16-bit WAV. The intended text is shown
questions: which sample sounds more like the person in the reference (1, 2, or no difference)
which sounds more natural (1, 2, or no difference)
which misread or garbled a word (1, 2, both, or none - an explicit answer)
delivery: one private web page, https://claude.ai/artifact/7yj1WvanE1A5pih2vLCMy7 (published 2026-10-03, source eval/runs/evidence/listening-v1/page.html): it interleaves both tests' 21 trials in one fixed order (seed 20261003), plays the clips as the builder wrote them (16-bit WAV, loudness-matched), asks the three questions per trial and names no test and no system. Listeners are asked to use headphones in a quiet room. The keys (which system is which sample) are in eval/runs/evidence/listening-v1/ and never on the page
listeners: the user recruits them. Planned: at least 5 - the analysis declared for a final result needs 5 listeners and 5 speakers; with fewer, only the exploratory interval is reported

analysis_fixed_before_listening.code: scripts/score_listening_test.py, per test, on the answers exported from the page in its responses format
analysis_fixed_before_listening.measures: for 'same person' and 'natural': the preference for system a (+1), b (-1) or no difference (0) per trial; misreads counted per system over answered trials
analysis_fixed_before_listening.intervals: over speakers (t interval, exploratory, conditional on these listeners) and, with at least 5 listeners, the two-way cluster bootstrap over speakers and listeners
what_would_be_concluded: OmniVoice against F5: a clear 'same person' preference for OmniVoice means the metric's large differences are audible; no preference would mean even a 0.11 similarity gap is not heard, and every similarity-based decision here would need rereading

published against adapted: the metric found no difference; 'no difference' from listeners agrees with it. A clear preference either way would be new and would call for a larger test before anything is claimed
misreads: whether listeners hear pronunciation differences the recogniser's CER does not show
analysis_fixed_before_listening.not_claimed: a handful of listeners from the user's circle is a first check, not a population; nothing is claimed beyond what the intervals say

built_by: scripts/build_listening_test.py (36ebe46) with --corpus-dir, --texts eval/manifests/test_texts_v1.json, the results files of the runs, --files and --bit-depth 16, seed 20261003
answers_are_kept: one record per listener: in the page's database as responses/<listener id> for anyone who can write there (the owner, and people invited by email as editors), each seeing only their own and the owner reading all; for anyone else, an answer code the page shows at the end, which they copy and send. Both turn into the scorer's files with scripts/export_listening_answers.py and the two keys
checked_before_listeners: 2026-10-03: all 63 audio files and the page are on the artifact; a probe record written as the owner was readable by the owner and hidden at a listener's level, then deleted. The user opened the page first, which saved their empty record
